scores.evidence: Critical path: access/IAM → M1 slice → template v1 stable (M2) → wave capacity (M3–M5) → legacy CI off
scores.rationale: Substrate (IAM/OIDC/ECR, Argo, chart) is built and proven with exit criteria before templates v1, waves, and enforcement; task dependencies are explicit.

scores.evidence: Pilot deployed to prod through the platform at least 5 times. Rollback timed under 10 minutes in staging and once in prod.
scores.rationale: M1 is a real thin slice to production on one real service before features like canary, Kyverno enforcement, or dashboards.

scores.evidence: D2 ... Reversibility: **Hard.** ... Revisit if: Services aren't on Kubernetes (A2), or there are more than about 10 clusters
scores.rationale: Decision table lists options, defaults, reversibility and revisit triggers, plus assumptions and open questions with defaults.

scores.evidence: Hardening: Argo CD HA, Kyverno audit mode ... Tier-1 migrations gated on the parity checklist; Wave 1: tier-3 and tier-2 ... Wave 2 tier-1
scores.rationale: Shared substrate (OIDC, ECR, Argo, chart) and the inventory precede migrations; within M1 tasks and template work are ordered by fan-out, and tier-1 leaf work is deferred until platform is hardened.

scores.evidence: Built in M1: GitHub OIDC to AWS with a push-only role ... M3: Kyverno verifyImages in audit mode ... M5: Kyverno switched to enforce mode
scores.rationale: Security has concrete content in M1 and every subsequent milestone (signing, audit, enforce, break-glass), not trailing.

scores.evidence: Built in M1: pipeline run duration and outcome per workflow and stage, exported to the existing metrics stack (T11). Argo CD Prometheus metrics.
scores.rationale: Metrics are in M1, dashboards/alerts in M3, canary analysis in M4, and enforcement-block monitoring in M5.

scores.evidence: Build once, promote the digest; Terraform state split by env; immutable tags; pinned semver templates; fixture harness
scores.rationale: Reproducibility (Terraform IaC, immutable digests, pinned templates, GitOps desired state) is present from M1 through later milestones.

scores.evidence: promote.yml waits for Argo health with a 15-minute timeout, then fails and alerts. It never retries a deploy blindly.
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in M1 (rollback drill, idempotent promote, health gate), M3 (HA, break-glass, load test), M4 (canary abort), and M5 (legacy fallback).

scores.evidence: AI-specific concerns: not applicable. There are no model-driven components.
scores.rationale: Plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Per-PR preview environments | Repeated staging contention or teams asking for them after M4
scores.rationale: Deferred table lists items with pull-forward triggers, plus deliberate shortcuts and M1 stubs with payback milestones.

note: Strong, well-sequenced plan; a real prod thin slice first, with security, observability, reproducibility and resilience in each milestone, explicit decision flip conditions, and deferred items with triggers. Only minor quibbles.
